21.page_title: Calling for self or someone else?
21.content:
Script

"Thank you for calling, I’m here to help you. Would you mind telling me how I can help?  

Is this call for yourself or someone else?"

📖  'IN CRISIS' is our shorthand for someone who feels that they are at risk of harming themselves (suicidal) or of harming others. 

    • Try not to use the word 'crisis' - instead, ask patients open-ended questions about what is concerning them (e.g., "what thoughts are going through your mind regarding your (or someone else's) safety?")
    • At the bottom of every card in this tree, there is a 'Patient in crisis' button.  If at any point in talking to the patient you feel that they are in crisis, you can just click this button to go directly to the MH Risk Assessment tree to assess them for more urgent care.


😶 If caller is reluctant to discuss the reason for the call ➡ select button 3 below.

🫂 If calling to discuss the mental health of another patient:

    • DO NOT give information out - you can receive information on behalf of a patient, but NOT share information without a patient's expressed permission.
    • Clarify the relationship between the caller and the patient.
    • Hide consultation notes (so patient can't see).
    • Record the name of the caller and the organisation (if call coming from another agency).
21.question: What is the reason for the call?
21.notes: Copied verbatim from 'Adult Mental Health' node 23

buttons.button_text: 1. ADULT calling for self or another adult - IN CRISIS
2. A person calling on behalf of a CHILD, or a child calling for self (includes IN CRISIS)
3. Adult calling for self or another adult for all other issues (NOT in crisis)

22.content:
Script

"What can I help you with today?"

The aim is to ask an open-ended question and then click the options listed. (i.e., do not read the red buttons out as a list).


If the patient is not specifically calling about:

  • addiction assistance, 
  • ADHD/autism, 
  • panic attacks, 
  • medication review, or 
  • review appointment, 

AND 

😶 they are reluctant to discuss the reason for calling ➡ select Speak to a clinician about their mental health button below.

25.content:
“To check that I book the right appointment, can I confirm if you are feeling safe at the moment?”

If the patient is unsure how to answer, you can rephrase the question to:

“Do you feel as though you're a risk to yourself or others?”


The safety question applies when the patient has not been seen before.

42.node_name: CYP - crisis lines + risk assessment intro
42.content:
Inform patient that you will send them these crisis line numbers before continuing to triage their symptoms. Confirm that they are happy to receive a text on their mobile number. The mobile number on EMIS may belong to a parent / guardian.


❇️ Crisis line contact information

SLaM Crisis number now NHS 111

On 1 April 2026, SLaM current 24/7 crisis line number for mental health crisis support (0800 731 2864) is transitioning to NHS 111. You’ll still reach the same local crisis teams - this change of numbers just makes it easier and quicker to access help through NHS 111. Anyone, of any age, experiencing a mental health crisis, or worried about a friend or family member, should call NHS 111 and select the mental health option after that time.


Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS) - 020 3228 5980


PRESS CONTINUE BELOW

✴️ Inform the patient that you will now complete a risk assessment with them. This is an important part of getting them the right care.

The questions may be repetitive but we are trying to gather as much information as possible.

52.content:
If the patient attends a primary or secondary school:

Advise the caller to discuss the situation with the school (nurse or SENCO). A referral for a diagnosis needs an assessment in school, and they can often provide more resources than a GP.

Note: SENCO is a teacher or staff member who has a special interest in coordinating special education needs and resources

Where school services may not be available (holidays, staffing restrictions etc), select the school unavailable option below.

61.content:
Script

“Before I ask more about the details, could I please ask you some yes/no questions to make sure you are (the person you are calling on behalf of is) safe at the moment? 

Some of them may not seem relevant to the current situation, but I need to ask these to work out how best to help.”



If the patient agrees:

Script

“Before we go through the yes/no questions together, I will send you a text with some helpful resources in case you need them. Can I please confirm the last 4 digits of your phone number?"


👉🏼 Actions to Note

💬 Send Accurx ➡ "Adult Mental Health Crisis"
